text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Clinton sweeps to easy victory: Support in large states key to Democrat's win: Dole's attacks on character issue fall short.
- Quebec Lieutenant-Governor quits over swastika admission: Bouchard urges post be scrapped.
- Tory MPP contradicts Ontario Premier Mike Harris on Ipperwash: Says office knew of police buildup in standoff with Indians at park.
- Doctors monitor Yeltsin after successful heart surgery: President could sign decree today to regain full powers.
- Former hockey great Gordie Howe tops list in NHL settlement.
- B.C. premier wants forestry hiring targets: Glen Clark would cut price of timber rights for companies that create jobs.
- Feeding frenzy hits bank stocks: Americans gobble up shares on strength of falling rates, rosy Morgan Stanley report.
- Court lifts freeze on Friedland's Inco shares: Ontario judge blasts 'shortcomings' of U.S. injunction case.
- Ads, scores and more coming to a phone screen near you: Bell Canada launches interactive service.
- Canadian auto sales surge: 41 percent rise in foreign-based models fuels double-digit growth.
- Financier Robert Friedland wins court battle: Ontario judge lifts freeze on US$152 million of financier's assets, blasts U.S. Justice Department for 'a material misrepresentation of the facts'
- Canadian Airlines was thrown into crisis when big investors shied away.
- Clinton gets second term with easy win.
